title: Local surjectivity of the truncated sheaf coproduct comparison
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $I$ be a set, $E_i\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category], and let $\iota_i:E_i\to S$ be an ambient coproduct in $D(\mathcal O_X)$. For every $a,q\in\mathbf Z$, the canonical sheaf morphism $\bigoplus_i H^q(Rf_*\tau_{\ge a}E_i)\to H^q(Rf_*\tau_{\ge a}S)$ is an epimorphism. Here $Rf_*$ is [def-pc-derived-direct-image]. This asserts local lifting of sections, without an affine global-section lifting assertion.

source.place: Tag 08DZ, bounded-below spectral-sequence paragraph, with Tag 015J

proof.text: Choose representatives and identify the cohomology of the ambient coproduct with the sums. Exact sums commute with canonical lower truncation and give the common bound a.

Apply natural bounded-below hypercohomology. On affine opens, qcqs cohomology of the inverse image commutes with sums; the higher-direct-image presheaf description and sheafification give second-page isomorphisms.
Maps of exact couples induce maps of pages. Exact sums preserve kernels, images and cokernels, so the second-page isomorphisms propagate to the stable pages.

In total degree q, only 0 <= p <= q-a occurs. Exact sums of the uniformly finite convergent filtrations have the corresponding sums as graded pieces. Finite filtration induction makes the canonical abutment comparison an isomorphism, hence epi. Naturality identifies Sigma.desc; below a and for the empty family both sides are zero.

theorem truncated_directImage_sheaf_coproduct_epi
    {X Y : Scheme.{u₁}} (f : X ⟶ Y) [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w₁} (SheafOfModules.{u₁} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w₂} (SheafOfModules.{u₁} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
    (I : Type u₁) (E : I → schemeDerivedQCohCategory X)
    (S : schemeDerivedCategory X) (ι : ∀ i, (E i).obj ⟶ S)
    (hc : IsColimit (Cofan.mk S ι)) (a q : ℤ) :
    Epi (Sigma.desc (fun i ↦ (schemeHigherDirectImage f q).map
      ((DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGE a).map (ι i))))
